issues.t: Transfer case locks up or fails
issues.sym: Binding or hopping in tight turns, clunks, a grinding or whining from under the middle of the SUV, a 4WD or service light, or the drivetrain locking up so the vehicle won't move freely.
issues.why: The transfer case splits power between the front and rear wheels on all-wheel-drive Rainiers. Owners report it wearing out internally or seizing at around 100,000+ miles, and it is the costliest problem reported for these SUVs.
issues.next: If the SUV binds or locks up, stop driving and have it towed. Ask the shop to check the transfer case fluid and the encoder motor first; a used or rebuilt transfer case is the usual fix if it has failed inside.

issues.t: Rear air suspension sags or the rear end drops
issues.sym: The back of the SUV sits low, especially after parking overnight, the compressor runs a lot or not at all, or the ride feels harsh and bottoms out over bumps.
issues.why: The self-leveling rear suspension uses rubber air springs and a small electric compressor. The air springs crack with age and leak, and the compressor wears out from running too often. Air suspension is the top Rainier repair in owner surveys.
issues.next: Have the air springs checked for leaks before replacing the compressor, or the new compressor will fail too. Some owners convert to regular coil springs and shocks.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold air
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air, or stops cooling altogether.
issues.why: Owners report the A/C system quitting at high mileage. A worn compressor or a refrigerant leak is the usual cause.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures checked and the system leak-tested before anyone just adds refrigerant. Fixing the leak or replacing the compressor is the lasting repair.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong or quits
issues.sym: The fuel gauge jumps around, sticks on full or empty, or the low-fuel light comes on at the wrong time.
issues.why: The fuel level sensor on the pump module inside the gas tank wears out and sends a bad reading to the gauge.
issues.next: Use the trip odometer to track your fuel until it is fixed so you don't run out. The repair usually means replacing the fuel level sender or the whole pump module.

issues.t: Cooling fan roars or engine runs hotter than normal
issues.sym: A loud roaring fan noise from the front of the engine even when it is not hot, slow or high-revving shifts, or the temperature gauge reading higher than usual.
issues.why: These SUVs use an electrically controlled fan clutch on the engine-driven fan. When it fails it can lock on and roar, or slip and let the engine run warm. GM issued bulletins for both the fan clutch noise and higher-than-normal temperature readings.
issues.next: If the gauge climbs toward hot, pull over and let the engine cool. Have the fan clutch and its wiring tested; replacing the fan clutch is a common fix.

issues.t: Flashing check engine light and misfire on the inline six
issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, a rough idle, shaking, or a loss of power.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for misfires and rough idle on the 4.2L six. Ignition coils, spark plugs and carbon on the valves are common causes.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Coil replacement is often the fix.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise from the engine that is loudest when cold, an exhaust smell, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The cast iron exhaust manifold cracks from repeated heating and cooling, and the bolts holding it on can break. Owners report it at around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the manifold inspected. Exhaust leaks near the engine can let fumes reach the cabin, so don't leave it for long.

issues.t: ABS and 4WD warning lights come on
issues.sym: The ABS light, sometimes together with the brake, traction or 4WD lights, stays on. On some trucks the heater blower also stops working at the same time.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins tracing these lights to a poor ground connection or wheel speed sensor circuit faults that the ABS module reports as communication errors.
issues.next: Normal braking still works, but anti-lock braking may not. Have the ABS codes read; cleaning and tightening the ground connection often fixes it.

issues.t: Battery keeps going dead
issues.sym: The SUV won't start after sitting, or the battery needs a jump again and again.
issues.why: Owners report repeated dead batteries. A battery past its life, a weak charging system or a module that stays awake and drains power are the usual causes.
issues.next: Have the battery and alternator tested first. If both are good, a shop can do a draw test to find what is draining power with the key off.

issues.t: Heater blower quits or won't shut off
issues.sym: The fan blows on only one speed, stops blowing, or keeps running after the SUV is turned off, sometimes only in very cold weather.
issues.why: The blower motor or its electronic speed control module wears out. GM issued a bulletin for blowers that stop or won't shut off in extreme cold.
issues.next: If the blower stays on with the key off it can drain the battery, so pull its fuse until it is fixed. The control module or motor is usually replaced.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hum
issues.sym: A humming or growling that rises with speed and may change when you steer left or right. The ABS light can come on if the bearing's speed sensor fails.
issues.why: The front wheel hub bearings wear out; owner surveys list them among the most common Rainier repairs.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked for play. A badly worn bearing can overheat or let the wheel wobble, so don't put it off.

issues.t: Front suspension clunks over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk, rattle or pop from the front when driving over rough roads or bumps.
issues.why: Worn front stabilizer bar links and bushings are a common source. GM issued bulletins for this rattle and a revised stabilizer part.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. Stabilizer links are quick to replace; also check tie rod ends, which wear on these SUVs too.

issues.t: Groan or shudder when turning at low speed
issues.sym: A moan, groan, chatter or shudder when making slow, tight turns, such as in parking lots.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for this noise on low-speed turns, and for chatter from the locking rear differential when turning.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check it against the bulletins. A fluid change in the differential or transfer case often helps.

issues.t: Outside door handle breaks
issues.sym: An outside door handle snaps, feels loose, or no longer opens the door.
issues.why: The plastic parts inside the handle break with use. Owners report this most on the 2006 model.
issues.next: Use another door until it is fixed. A new handle can be painted to match.

issues.t: Gas pump shuts off early when filling up
issues.sym: The pump nozzle keeps clicking off before the tank is full, or fuel spits back out of the filler.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for hard filling. A problem in the fuel tank vent or vapor recovery system keeps air from leaving the tank fast enough.
issues.next: Try filling at a slower rate. If it keeps happening, have the vent and vapor system checked, since a fault there can also set a check engine light.

issues.t: Check engine light for an evaporative leak
issues.sym: A check engine light with a fuel vapor leak code. There is usually no change in how the SUV drives.
issues.why: The system that stores fuel vapors from the tank has a leak, often at the gas cap, a vent valve or a cracked hose. GM issued a bulletin on diagnosing these codes.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks tight. If the light returns, a shop can smoke-test the system to find the leak.

issues.t: Power steering fluid leak at the steering gear
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips near the left front wheel, the fluid level drops, or the steering whines.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for a leaking seal on the steering gear's output (pitman) shaft.
issues.next: Keep the fluid topped up and have the leak checked. Replacing the seal or the steering gear fixes it; running the pump low on fluid can damage it.

issues.t: Brakes squeak when pressing or releasing the pedal
issues.sym: A squeak or squeegee sound when you press or let off the brake pedal.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for brake squeak on these SUVs. Pad material, worn hardware and dry contact points are common causes.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected to make sure the pads are not worn out. Cleaning and lubricating the pad hardware, or new pads, usually stops the noise.

issues.t: Driver's power window switch can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Windows or locks that work on and off, a burning smell, or smoke or melting at the driver's door switch, even with the SUV parked and off.
issues.why: Fluid can get into the driver's master window switch and short the circuit board. GM recalled these SUVs several times; an earlier fix added a protective coating, and a later recall was needed because the coating did not remove the risk.
issues.next: Check with a Buick dealer using your VIN. Until the recall is done, park outside and away from buildings.

issues.t: Headlights can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The low beams flicker or go out, often one side at a time, while driving.
issues.why: The headlamps could stop lighting because of an electrical fault. GM recalled about 429,000 SUVs in 2015 to fix it.
issues.next: If your headlights go out, pull over safely and use other lights. Ask a Buick dealer whether the recall repair has been done on your VIN.

issues.t: Power steering hose can fail (recall)
issues.sym: A power steering fluid leak, a whining pump, and then steering that suddenly gets heavy. On some SUVs braking also gets harder.
issues.why: A power steering hose could fail. On versions that use power steering fluid to boost the brakes, a failure can also cut brake assist.
issues.next: If the steering gets heavy, slow down and stop safely. Have a dealer confirm the recall hose was replaced.

issues.t: Tire information label has wrong data (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; the tire and loading label on the door frame shows wrong numbers.
issues.why: A misprinted label could lead owners to load the SUV wrong or set the wrong tire pressure.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN and replace the label. Use the pressures in the owner's manual in the meantime.

issues.t: Windshield may not be held in properly (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom you would notice; the windshield adhesive may not have bonded properly at the factory.
issues.why: On some SUVs the windshield urethane did not stick as it should, so the glass might not stay in place in a crash.
issues.next: Have a Buick dealer check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Brake lights and rear turn signals may fail (recall)
issues.sym: The brake lights or rear turn signals stop working.
issues.why: A defect could keep the brake lamps and rear turn signals from working, so drivers behind you get no warning that you are stopping or turning.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights. Ask a Buick dealer whether the recall was completed.

issues.t: Turn signals may not work (recall)
issues.sym: The turn signals stop working or act strangely.
issues.why: A turn signal fault could stop the driver from signaling turns or lane changes, or from warning others with the hazards.
issues.next: Use hand signals if needed and get the recall done at a Buick dealer.
